title: RCMP defend sending lone officer to disturbance
article: The spokesman for the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team is standing behind the decision to have a lone female RCMP officer attend a call in a South Surrey neighbourhood that ended with 46-year-old David Stitt's death in hospital Thursday.

Corporal Dale Carr said that if the RCMP is to properly manage its resources, officers cannot always wait for backup that might be deemed unnecessary. If one officer believes he or she can sufficiently handle a call, Cpl. Carr said, it makes sense for that officer to attempt to do so.
On Tuesday, just before midnight, Surrey RCMP received a complaint of a disturbance in the 13500 block of Crescent Road.

The first officer on the scene observed Mr. Stitt in an agitated state. She attempted to strike up a conversation with him, but Mr. Stitt, according to an IHIT news release, came at her with what's believed to have been a broomstick.
The officer took out her pepper spray, but Mr. Stitt continued to advance. Now locked in a physical confrontation, the officer struck Mr. Stitt in the lower body with her defence baton.
Two men, one who lives in the neighbourhood and another who was driving by, came to the officer's aid and helped subdue the suspect.
As a handcuffed Mr. Stitt was escorted to a police cruiser, he collapsed. CPR was administered and he was admitted to a local hospital where he died the following day.
An autopsy was conducted yesterday, and Cpl. Carr expects the findings to be released in two to three months.

Sergeant Roger Morrow of the Surrey RCMP said Wednesday that police rely on the information provided by the person making a complaint to assess how many officers are needed for a call. For a disturbance complaint, one officer can be deemed enough.

The Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP is overseeing the IHIT investigation. Cpl. Carr asserted that if the commission deems any aspect of the investigation to be flawed, that aspect will be corrected immediately.

Friends of Mr. Stitt, or "Painter Dave" as he was called because of his job, have created a Facebook group in his memory. Shane Brown described him as "the funniest, most caring lovable and great all-around guy." Danielle Viher expressed shock at the violent portrayal of Mr. Stitt, saying "it sounds nothing like the Painter Dave I remember."
